methodological_rigor.justification: Study employs sound in vitro design with appropriate controls (Q-VD-OPh, olaparib) and multiple DLBCL lines. However, findings rely predominantly on SU-DHL-10 (double-hit lymphoma model) which the authors acknowledge limits generalizability to major DLBCL subtypes (GCB, ABC). No in vivo validation or patient-derived cells. ANOVA with Tukey post hoc testing is appropriate, but power calculation is absent and confidence intervals not reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical cell-line study maps to Oxford LoE 5. Identifies novel PARP1-mediated parthanatos pathway with potential for R/R DLBCL, but translational relevance is speculative. Authors extensively discuss bioavailability challenges (0.8% oral bioavailability), lack of animal models, and absence of stratified analysis across patient subtypes, limiting near-term clinical application.

reporting_quality.justification: Detailed Methods section describes cell culture, drug preparation, thawing protocols, CCK-8, Western blot, immunofluorescence, and statistical analysis following preclinical reporting standards. Results presented with clear figures and legends; Discussion addresses study limitations. Major gap: no Data Availability statement, no mention of raw data or code sharing. Compliance with ARRIVE is thorough for reported elements.

novelty_literature.justification: First demonstration of curcumin-induced parthanatos in DLBCL cells and first report of curcumin-UVB synergy via this pathway. Parthanatos is established in other malignancies and curcumin's antitumor activity is known, but combination and mechanism in DLBCL represent novel contribution. Authors claim 'to the best of our knowledge, the present study is the first report demonstrating curcumin-induced activation of the parthanatos pathway in DLBCL cells.'

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured narrative with clear introduction positioning work in TCM context and unmet DLBCL needs. Methods systematically organized. Results logically progress from dose-response to mechanism validation to combination effects. Discussion thoroughly addresses limitations, including cell-line restriction and need for primary cells. Figures effectively communicate nuclear translocation and PAR accumulation. Professional prose with accurate scientific terminology.

key_strengths: Novel demonstration of curcumin-induced PARP1-mediated parthanatos in DLBCL, filling a documented mechanistic gap and offering alternative cell-death pathway for apoptosis-resistant models
Rigorous mechanistic validation using complementary approaches (Western blot, immunofluorescence, DAPI/PI staining) with selective PARP inhibition (olaparib) confirming parthanatos dependence
Strong experimental controls including caspase inhibitor Q-VD-OPh to distinguish apoptosis-independent pathway and detailed characterization of cell-line baseline phenotypes

Honest, comprehensive discussion of limitations including restriction to double-hit lymphoma model, generalizability concerns across DLBCL subtypes, and substantial bioavailability barriers to translation
key_concerns: Preclinical cell-line only (LoE 5); primary findings driven by SU-DHL-10, which is non-representative of major DLBCL subtypes (germinal center B-cell, activated B-cell), severely limiting clinical relevance
No in vivo efficacy data or animal models; authors acknowledge need for patient-derived xenograft or humanized models but provide none

Critical bioavailability gap: curcumin oral bioavailability <1% with rapid first-pass metabolism—authors acknowledge but present no delivery optimization, making clinical translation highly speculative
Missing Data Availability statement; no indication of raw data, code, or materials sharing, limiting reproducibility and replication
UVB irradiation used as DNA-damage surrogate for radiotherapy, but protocol parameters differ between cell lines (60 vs. 120 sec), raising reproducibility concerns
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid preclinical mechanistic study with novel parthanatos pathway discovery and appropriate controls, but limited to cell-line model of unrepresentative DLBCL subtype with substantial bioavailability and translational barriers acknowledged but unaddressed. Suitable for Tier 3 (Cancers, Frontiers Oncology, BMC Cancer) with minor revisions addressing data availability and reproducibility details; not ready for Tier 1-2 venues due to preclinical-only design and generalizability limits.
